chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihrān, may Allah have mercy on him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the status of the Imams?
He عليه السلام said: Like the status of Dhū al-Qarnayn, and like the status of Yūshaʿ, and like the status of Āṣaf, the companion of Sulaymān.

He said: Then by what do you judge? He عليه السلام said: By the judgment of Allah, and the judgment of the family of Dāwūd, and the judgment of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the Holy Spirit conveys it to us.

key_terms.آصَفَ: Āṣaf, the companion of Sulaymān known for divinely granted knowledge
key_terms.آلِ دَاوُدَ: the family of Dāwūd, associated with divinely guided judgment
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams, the divinely appointed leaders
key_terms.حُكْمِ اللَّهِ: the judgment of Allah as the basis of ruling
key_terms.ذِي الْقَرْنَيْنِ: Dhū al-Qarnayn, cited as a model of elevated station
key_terms.رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ: the Holy Spirit through whom this knowledge is conveyed
key_terms.يُوشَعَ: Yūshaʿ, mentioned as a figure of special rank

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kāfī say about the status of the Imams and the source of their judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the exalted rank of the Imams by comparing their station to figures endowed with divine authority and special knowledge. It also states that their judgment is based on the judgment of Allah, the family of Dāwūd, and Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, received through Rūḥ al-Qudus.
